cues.zh: 大约20年前——快20年前，我在一家小型社会服务非营利组织工作
cues.en: So 20 years ago -- almost 20 years ago, I was working for a small social service non-profit

cues.zh: 为无家可归的家庭提供无家可归者服务和住房。
cues.en: that provided homeless services and housing to homeless families.

cues.zh: 就是在那里，我遇到了一位女士，我打算叫她Julia。
cues.en: And that is where I met a woman that I'm going to call Julia.

cues.zh: 她是一位单亲母亲。
cues.en: She was a single mother.

cues.zh: 她有三个儿子。
cues.en: She had three sons.

cues.zh: 她住在我们的一栋楼里。
cues.en: She was living in one of our buildings.

cues.zh: Julia其实——我们曾希望她是一个巨大的成功案例。
cues.en: Julia was actually -- we hoped a great success story.

cues.zh: 她之前一直借住别人家沙发，做着很多无家可归家庭会做的事，也就是
cues.en: So she had been couch surfing, doing a lot of what homeless families do in terms of moving

cues.zh: 从一个不稳定的处境搬到另一个不稳定的处境。
cues.en: from unstable situation to unstable situation.

cues.zh: 我们帮她安顿进了一套稳定、永久的公寓；帮她找到了一份工作，一份不错的
cues.en: We'd gotten got her situated in a stable, permanent apartment; gotten her a job, a good

cues.zh: 清洁工工作。
cues.en: job as a janitor.

cues.zh: 这听起来可能对你们不算什么，但这份工作的薪水超过
cues.en: And it probably doesn't sound like much to you but this was a job that paid more than

cues.zh: 最低工资的两倍，有晋升机会，还有福利，包括医疗和
cues.en: twice minimum wage, had opportunity for advancement, and have benefits, including health and a

cues.zh: 养老金。
cues.en: pension.

cues.zh: 对长期领福利、没受过多少教育的人来说，这是份好工作。
cues.en: This was a good job for someone who had been on long-term welfare, didn't have a lot of

cues.zh: 教育。
cues.en: education.

cues.zh: 有一条通往中产的路，这正是我们希望穷人能有的，对吧？
cues.en: There was a path to the middle class, which is what we want for the poor, right?

cues.zh: 说到底，这就是在座每个人——这就是全美国每个人希望
cues.en: Ultimately, it's what everyone in this room -- it's what everyone in America wants for

cues.zh: 穷人能拥有的：一条通往中产的路，通往稳定和掌控命运，
cues.en: the poor is a path to the middle class, to the stability and the destiny, the self-control,

cues.zh: 掌控自己命运的能力，为自己建立家园和生活。
cues.en: the ability to control your own destiny, to build a place and a life for yourself.

cues.zh: 然后——Julia本来干得挺好，后来她妹妹失去了房子。
cues.en: And then -- so Julia was doing really well and then her sister lost her house.

cues.zh: 她妹妹有个年幼的儿子，Julia收留了外甥，然后她辞了工作，
cues.en: Her sister had an infant son and Julia took in her nephew and then she quit her job and

cues.zh: 领了九个月福利，就为了照顾妹妹的儿子。
cues.en: went on welfare for nine months in order to care of her sister's son.

cues.zh: 九个月后，妹妹终于稳定下来，能把儿子接回去了，
cues.en: Nine months later, when her sister finally got stable, was able to take her son back,

cues.zh: 却已经没有保洁岗位空缺了。
cues.en: there wasn't a janitorial job available.

cues.zh: 她得到的工作是在K-Mart。
cues.en: The job that she got was at K-Mart.

cues.zh: 那份工作拿的是最低工资，当时是每小时4.25美元，而且从那里往上晋升的机会相当有限。
cues.en: It paid minimum wage, which was then $4.25 an hour, and there is pretty limited opportunity

cues.zh: 非常有限。
cues.en: for advancement from there.

cues.zh: 你知道，当时我作为一个22岁还住在家里的秘书，评判心挺重的。
cues.en: And, you know, at the time, I was pretty judgy for a 22-year-old secretary who was still

cues.zh: 还住在家里。
cues.en: living at home.

cues.zh: 我无法理解她怎么会这么做，她——她怎么能这么蠢。
cues.en: I couldn't understand how she had done this, how she -- how she could be so stupid.

cues.zh: 我当时就想——而我做了很多中产阶级的人在听到这类故事时会做的事，
cues.en: I was like -- and I did what a lot of middle-class people do when they hear stories like this,

cues.zh: 就是把它归咎于——她判断力差，或者也许她没有
cues.en: which is that I attributed it to bad -- she had bad judgment or maybe she didn't have

cues.zh: 良好的职业道德，决策能力差，对吧，激励不当。
cues.en: a good work ethic, poor decision-making skills, right, bad incentives.

cues.zh: 我花了20年时间，还写了一本关于失败的书，才明白这从根本上
cues.en: It took me 20 years and writing a book about failures to understand that this was fundamentally

cues.zh: 跟那些都无关，从根本上说，她所做的一切关乎资本，而
cues.en: about none of those things, that fundamentally what she was doing was about capital and that

cues.zh: 如果我们想帮助穷人爬上那道阶梯进入中产阶级，进入这个房间里每个人都享有的
cues.en: if we want to help the poor climb that ladder into the middle class, into the stable, bourgeois

cues.zh: 稳定的资产阶级生活，那我们就需要解决这个问题。
cues.en: life that everyone in this room enjoys, then we need to address this problem.

cues.zh: 这是机遇、稳定和美国梦对数百万仍在努力向上攀爬的穷人来说意味着什么的核心所在
cues.en: This is at the core of what opportunity and stability and the American dream is going

cues.zh: 对数百万人来说，这就是机遇、稳定和美国梦的意义所在，他们仍在努力攀爬那架梯子。
cues.en: to mean for millions of poor people who are still trying to climb that ladder.

cues.zh: 要理解原因，我想先绕道去一趟巴拉圭的雨林。
cues.en: To see why, I want to take a little detour into the rain forests of Paraguay.

cues.zh: 我发誓这后面是有道理的，请耐心听我说。
cues.en: I swear to God this is going somewhere, so please bear with me.

cues.zh: 在巴拉圭，有一个叫 Aché 的部落，他们在那里的历史已经非常
cues.en: So in Paraguay, there is a tribe called the Aché, and they have been there for a very

cues.zh: 很久以来，比我们有文字记载的历史还要久。
cues.en: long time, for longer than we have written history.

cues.zh: 在那大部分时间里，他们都是觅食者，也就是你们可能认为的狩猎采集者。
cues.en: And for most of that time, they have been foragers, what you probably think of as hunter-gatherers.

cues.zh: 狩猎采集者真的很有意思，因为他们共享很多东西。
cues.en: So hunter-gathers are really interesting because hunter-gatherers share a lot.

cues.zh: 他们共享的远比我们多，这很有意思，因为你想，这是
cues.en: They share way more than we do which is interesting because you think about this is the first

cues.zh: 我们进化成人类之后采取的第一种生活方式，而黑猩猩根本不
cues.en: kind of lifestyle that we adopted after we evolved into humans, and chimps don't share

cues.zh: 共享。
cues.en: at all.

cues.zh: 但狩猎采集者基本上是我们所知最乐于分享的社会。
cues.en: But the hunter-gatherers are basically the most sharing societies that we know.

cues.zh: 这其实是有原因的。
cues.en: There's actually a reason for this.

cues.zh: 他们拥有的不是财产，而是所谓的互惠利他。
cues.en: Instead of property, what they have is what you call reciprocal altruism.

cues.zh: 你可以在自己的生活中看到这一点，比如说，你妈妈让你在回家路上带一加仑
cues.en: So you can see this in our own life is, say, your mother asks you to pick up a gallon of

cues.zh: 牛奶给她。
cues.en: milk for her on the way home.

cues.zh: 我去杂货店买一加仑牛奶时，不会给我妈
cues.en: When I go to the grocery store and I pick up a gallon of milk, I don't send my mother

cues.zh: 寄账单，对吧？
cues.en: a bill, right?

cues.zh: 我只是想着她以后总会还我人情。
cues.en: I just figure she's going to get me back later at some point.

cues.zh: 我需要鸡蛋时，她会送过来，等等。
cues.en: I'll need eggs, she'll bring them by, et cetera.

cues.zh: 这就是互惠利他，每个人都会做一点。
cues.en: That's reciprocal altruism and everyone does it a little bit.

cues.zh: 你主要在家庭关系中这么做，也许对朋友或同事也会。
cues.en: You do it within your family relationships mostly, maybe for friends or coworkers.

cues.zh: 但对我们来说，这些关系非常有限，而且都是些小恩小惠，
cues.en: But for us, these relationships are very narrowly limited and they're also small-ticket items,

cues.zh: 对吧？
cues.en: right?

cues.zh: 很少有人会说，嘿，妈，我给你买了辆车。
cues.en: Very few people are like, hey, mom, I bought you car.

cues.zh: 不用还我钱。
cues.en: No need to pay me back.

cues.zh: 你以后再还我就行。
cues.en: You'll just get me later.

cues.zh: 但对阿切人来说，这要核心得多。
cues.en: But for the Aché, it's much more central.

cues.zh: 对狩猎采集者整体而言，这在他们的社会和经济生活中要核心得多得多。
cues.en: For hunter-gatherers in general, it is much, much more central to their social and economic

cues.zh: 生活。
cues.en: life.

cues.zh: 有意思的是。
cues.en: So here's the interesting thing.

cues.zh: 阿切人其实不得不停止做采集者，原因和许多原住民
cues.en: The Aché actually had to stop being foragers for the same reason that a lot of indigenous

cues.zh: 一样——供养一个采集者需要大量土地，而随着农民侵占
cues.en: people have had to -- it takes a lot of territory to support a forager, and as farmers encroached

cues.zh: 雨林，他们最终不得不定居下来成为农民。
cues.en: on the rain forest, they ended up having to settle down to be farmers.

cues.zh: 当他们定居下来——为写书我采访了一位目睹这一过程的人类学家，
cues.en: And when they settled down -- and for my book I interviewed an anthropologist who watched

cues.zh: 他在这一过程中与阿切人共事——当他们定居下来
cues.en: this process, who worked with the Aché during this process -- when they settled down to

cues.zh: 成为农民后，他们不再那么频繁地分享了。
cues.en: be farmers, they stopped sharing so much.

cues.zh: 阿切人即使在采集者中也以分享程度之高而格外突出。
cues.en: The Aché were actually even among foragers remarkable for the degree to which they shared.

cues.zh: 他们有一条规范：男人不能吃自己杀死的肉。
cues.en: They had a norm that men could not eat meat that they themselves had killed.

cues.zh: 他们告诉——他们告诉那些人，如果这么做，就会——就会失去
cues.en: They told -- they told the guys that if they did, they would -- they would lose their ability

cues.zh: 打猎的能力，我觉得这有点像告诉一个美国人你会失去
cues.en: to hunt, which I guess is kind of like telling an American guy that you're going to lose

cues.zh: 看超级碗的能力，于是他们就分享了。
cues.en: your ability to watch the Super Bowl, and so they shared.

cues.zh: 他们从不吃自己的猎物。
cues.en: They never ate from their own kill.

cues.zh: 他们广泛地分享给不在家庭圈子里的人，那些人属于
cues.en: They shared widely with people who were not in their family circle, who were in their

cues.zh: 更大的约50人的群体——他们一直与之生活的50到150人。
cues.en: larger band of about 50 people that they were -- 50 to 150 people they'd been living with.

cues.zh: 于是他们定居下来，然后就不再这样了。
cues.en: So they settled down and then they stopped.

cues.zh: 他们仍然会进森林，但渐渐地分享变少了，而在农场上他们
cues.en: They're still going into the forest, but gradually they're sharing less, and on the farm they're

cues.zh: 分享得更少。
cues.en: sharing even less.

cues.zh: Kaplan 对此有一套理论。
cues.en: And Kaplan had a theory for this.

cues.zh: 首先，他说，它失败的原因和集体农庄失败的原因一样。
cues.en: So, first of all, he said, it failed for the reason that collective farms fail.

cues.zh: 如果你看看普利茅斯殖民地，或者俄罗斯，集体农庄行不通
cues.en: If you look at the Plymouth colony or for that matter Russia, collective farms didn't

cues.zh: 原因大致相同。
cues.en: work for much the same reason.

cues.zh: 他们会敲钟把人召集起来下地干活，就像他们当初
cues.en: They would ring a bell to gather people together to go into the fields the way that they had

cues.zh: 试图进入森林那样，而正如 Kaplan 所说，没人出现。
cues.en: tried to go into the forest and, as Kaplan said, no one turned up.

cues.zh: 于是，他们最终在十年内建立了产权，这种价值观对他们来说
cues.en: So, instead, they ended up with property rights in a span of 10 years, a value that was as

cues.zh: 就像美国人的价值观一样重要——比如“这是我的草坪，未经我允许
cues.en: important to them as the American value of like that's my lawn and don't step on it unless

cues.zh: 别踩上来”，不过我觉得侵入邻居家的蒲公英地是合法的
cues.en: I give you permission, although I think it is legal to invade your neighbor had dandelions

cues.zh: ——或者说应该是合法的。
cues.en: -- or should be.

cues.zh: 但总的来说，这种价值观对他们来说同样神圣，就像产权
cues.en: But, in general, this was a value that was just as sacred to them as property rights

cues.zh: 对我们一样，而它在十年内就改变了，在非常短的时间内。
cues.en: are to us and it changed in 10 years, in a very brief span of time.

cues.zh: 为什么？
cues.en: Why?

cues.zh: Kaplan 对此有个理论，听起来很有道理，而且他后来确实在实验中验证过
cues.en: Kaplan had a theory about this that rings true and that he's actually subsequently tested

cues.zh: 这个理论是：分享适合狩猎采集，不适合农耕。
cues.en: in experiments, which is that sharing is appropriate to foraging and it's not to farming.

cues.zh: 原因如下。
cues.en: And here's why.

cues.zh: 想想猎人是如何工作的。
cues.en: So think about how a hunter works.

cues.zh: 你在猎海豹，对吧？
cues.en: You're hunting a seal right?

cues.zh: 你到冰洞口，等着海豹出现。
cues.en: You go to an ice hole and you wait for a seal to show up.

cues.zh: 你可能是全世界最厉害的猎人，是狩猎采集界的超人；但如果
cues.en: You can be the best hunter in the entire world, the superman of foraging or hunting; if a

cues.zh: 海豹不出现，你今天就没饭吃。
cues.en: seal doesn't show up, you're not going to eat today.

cues.zh: 与此同时，你一英里半外的朋友在另一个洞口，可能拥有
cues.en: Meanwhile, your friend, who's a mile and a half away at a different hole, may have hundreds

cues.zh: 几十万卡路里，远超他和家人能消耗的量。
cues.en: of thousands of calories more than he and his family could possibly consume.

cues.zh: Kaplan 的意思是，分享就像资本。
cues.en: What Kaplan is saying is that sharing is like capital.

cues.zh: 它是一种储蓄。
cues.en: It's saving.

cues.zh: 当你生活在勉强糊口的水平，无法储蓄，因为你只能带走
cues.en: When you live at a subsistence level, where you can't save because you can only take what

cues.zh: 你能随身携带的东西，你拥有的替代品就是这种社会互助保险。
cues.en: you can carry with you, what you have instead is this form of social insurance.

cues.zh: 我现在给你一些东西；我和你分享我的食物；以后我需要的时候，你也会分享
cues.en: I give you something now; I share my food with you; later, when I need, you will share

cues.zh: 给我。
cues.en: with me.

cues.zh: 这是一种开放式的义务。
cues.en: It's an open-ended obligation.

cues.zh: 它是双向的。
cues.en: It's bilateral.

cues.zh: 这一点真的非常非常重要。
cues.en: This is really, really important.

cues.zh: 那么，好吧。
cues.en: So, okay.

cues.zh: 你可能会问，这和 Julia 有什么关系？
cues.en: What does this have to do with Julia, you may be asking?

cues.zh: 美国的穷人所拥有的金融资本非常有限——基本上没有。
cues.en: The poor in America have very limited financial capital -- basically none.

cues.zh: 如果你看看美国社会底层的差不多一半人，粗略来说，
cues.en: If you look at the bottom sort of half of American society, to a first approximation,

cues.zh: 他们的净财富为零。
cues.en: they have zero net wealth.

cues.zh: 所以当你听到沃尔顿家族拥有的财富比底层40%的人还多这个统计数据时，
cues.en: So when you hear the statistic that the Waltons have more wealth than like the bottom 40 percent,

cues.zh: 恭喜——你们大多数人也是如此。
cues.en: congratulations -- most of you do too.

cues.zh: 所以只要你的资产超过负债1美元，你就比大约
cues.en: So as long as your assets exceed your liabilities by $1, you're doing better than about the

cues.zh: 美国社会底层四分之一的人过得更好。
cues.en: bottom quarter of American society.

cues.zh: 那么，当你没有任何金融资本时，你需要什么？
cues.en: So what do you need when you don't have any financial capital?

cues.zh: 在美国，贫穷的讽刺之处在于，如果你有一点资本，贫穷会容易得多
cues.en: The irony of being poor in America is that it's a lot easier to be poor if you have a

cues.zh: 一点点资本。
cues.en: little bit of capital.

cues.zh: 你不需要很多。
cues.en: You don't need much.

cues.zh: 但一点点资本就能做到比如给你付公寓的押金
cues.en: But a little bit of capital can do things like give you the deposit on an apartment

cues.zh: 这样你就不必按天或按周租汽车旅馆房间，那比月租
cues.en: so that you don't have to rent a motel room by the night or the week, which is much more

cues.zh: 贵得多。
cues.en: expensive than monthly rent.

cues.zh: 你还可以做这样的事，帮你买车，让你能搬到郊区更好的房子和更好的
cues.en: And you do things like help you buy a car so you can get to a better house and better

cues.zh: 学区，或者如果你住在市里，能去郊区上班。
cues.en: school district in the suburbs or to get to a job in the suburbs if you live in the city.

cues.zh: 它能让你买一辆可靠的8000美元的车，而不是一辆500美元、每四个月就要花1500美元
cues.en: It can let you buy a reliable $8,000 car instead of a $500 car that needs $1,500 worth or repairs

cues.zh: 修的车。
cues.en: every four months.

cues.zh: 你有没有见过那种房子，车道上停着五辆破车，而不是
cues.en: Have you ever seen that house that has like five beat-up cars parked in the driveway instead

cues.zh: 两辆车况还不错的车？
cues.en: of two pretty good condition ones?

cues.zh: 拥有那些车的人并不愚蠢。
cues.en: The people who own those cars aren't stupid.

cues.zh: 他们买那些便宜车，是因为没有足够的钱去买一辆可靠的车，而且
cues.en: They have those cheap cars because they didn't have enough money to buy a reliable car and

cues.zh: 他们需要五辆，才能确保有一两辆能随时准备好，在他们该去上班的时候
cues.en: they need five to make sure that one or two will be ready to take them to work when it's

cues.zh: 真正能开动。
cues.en: time to go and actually running.

cues.zh: 拥有资本，你就能办Costco会员，也许还能买个卧式冰柜，用来装那900
cues.en: Having capital allows you to have Costco membership and maybe buy a chest freezer for the 900

cues.zh: 磅猪肩肉——当你看到他们肉柜里的东西时，你肯定会忍不住带回家
cues.en: pounds of pork butt that you will inevitably bring home when you get a look at their meat

cues.zh: 塞满冰柜。
cues.en: freezer.

cues.zh: 资本还能让你去做一些事，比如支付牙科护理费用，买能让你获得
cues.en: It also allows you to do things like buy dental care and clothes that can enable you to get

cues.zh: 更好工作的衣服。
cues.en: a better job.

cues.zh: 但最重要的，也许是拥有一小笔资本，能让你免于
cues.en: But, most importantly, probably, is having a small amount of capital protects from having

cues.zh: 还有数百万人也能做到。
cues.en: Millions more can.

cues.zh: 我们可以帮助世界上的朱莉娅们摆脱那种为了帮妹妹而不得不辞职的处境，
cues.en: We can help the Julias of the world get out of a place where she needs to quit her job

cues.zh: 让她们处在一个大家都有足够积蓄渡过难关的地方，
cues.en: in order to help her sister out and in a place where everyone has enough to tide them over

cues.zh: 渡过那些灾难性的危机。
cues.en: those catastrophic crises.

cues.zh: 说到这里，我就结束了。
cues.en: And, with that, I will close.

cues.zh: 谢谢大家。
cues.en: And thank you.

cues.zh: 感谢观看。
cues.en: Thanks for watching.

cues.zh: 我们很想听听你对抗击贫困的看法，请在下方评论区告诉我们。
cues.en: We'd love to hear what you think about fighting poverty, so tell us in the comments below.

cues.zh: 然后请帮我们传播，分享这个视频。
cues.en: Then please help us spread the word by sharing this video.

cues.zh: 想看更多愿景演讲，请点击订阅按钮并访问网站 ThePursuitOfHappiness.com。
cues.en: For more vision talks click the subscribe button and visit the website ThePursuitOfHappiness.com.
